newsitem.title: UK: NWE diesel demand rises, Russia-U.S. arb opens.
newsitem.headline: NWE diesel demand rises, Russia-U.S. arb opens.

text.p: A duel between two trading houses over the Nov IPE continued to stifle barge market liquidity on Friday but cargoes perked up with an arb opening for Russian to the United States, traders said.
Traders said a surge in French demand for low sulphur diesel lent a further sign of life to a market muted by a bad-tempered dispute over the November IPE gas oil futures delivery.

Dec IPE firmed $3.75 to $222.75 a tonne, cathing up Brent's late Thursday rally. A barge of heating oil was traded unchanged at Dec IPE +2 for late Nov but traders said activity was almost paralysed by the Nov IPE play involving over 600,000 tonnes.

AIC, the dominant Nov short, has said Cargill, the main long, did not take full delivery in the first of three five-day delivery periods and on Friday it added Cargill was slow with nominations on the second window.
Cargill had no immediate comment on the second charge.

Traders said Russian premiums were steady to firm at around Dec Ipe +$5/7 with an arb to New York now open. Heating oil caroges were steady at Dec IPE +$5/6. A low sulphur diesel was rumoured bid at Dec +$17 into Le Havre.
